summary: We developed AETHER-Care, an end-to-end, zero-burden health and behavioral monitoring system designed for long-duration deep space missions (such as Mars or Artemis lunar missions). It addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge by eliminating the heavy reliance on astronaut self-reporting and bulky, uncomfortable medical gear. Using a dual-mode ambient and embedded architecture, it continuously monitors cardiovascular, respiratory, thermal, and cognitive health without skin friction or workflow disruption. It is crucial because it ensures crew safety, protects astronaut privacy through local Edge AI, and autonomously overrides for medical emergencies when communication with Earth is delayed.
details:
AETHER-Care operates in two distinct modes:

Cabin Mode (Contactless): Uses TI IWR6843AOP 60GHz mmWave radar and FLIR Lepton 3.5 thermal/rPPG cameras to silently monitor heart rate (HR), respiration rate (RR), HRV, and skin temperature while astronauts sleep or work at consoles.

EVA Suit Mode (3–4 Day Missions): Integrates ultra-thin graphene dry-textile electrodes (MAX30001/MAX86150), Bosch BME688 helmet gas/CO₂ sensors, and Bosch BMI270 IMU motion trackers into the LCVG underwear and helmet.

Passive Mental Health Assessment: Eliminates NASA's boring 3-minute PVT tests by passively analyzing keystroke dynamics, vocal acoustic biomarkers, and micro-blinking during routine daily tasks.

Edge AI & Privacy: Powered by an STM32U585 microcontroller running quantized TinyML/SLMs locally. All psychological data remains encrypted in an on-device privacy vault, while critical medical thresholds trigger an autonomous emergency telemetry override.

Tools, Languages & Hardware: Python, C++, TinyML, TensorFlow Lite, TI IWR6843AOP, FLIR Lepton 3.5, Analog Devices MAX86150, Bosch BME688, Bosch BMI270, and STM32U5.

Benefits & Goals: Reduces hardware weight by 85%, cuts power consumption by 70%, saves 100% of astronaut test time, and provides proactive dual-use protection for space exploration and terrestrial ICUs.
